# Original interrupted statistics receive cases

Five current original-only executions were captured before native controller
implementation, using the unchanged Python source, actual original msgq/Params
and a freshly compiled `zmq_receive_boundary.c` preload. Captured results cover
one/repeated EINTR, EINTR followed by EAGAIN, EINVAL and ENOTSOCK. No expected
result was generated by the native statsd candidate. The C source and Python
inputs are pinned in source-pins.json; the exact original fixture bytes are
pinned in the permanent tests. Private raw evidence and shim hashes are under
`.analysis/scratch/2026-10-19-stats-interrupted-tools/`.

The native `check-stats-interrupted` controller now compares these five sealed
source results with actual link-wrapped native daemon executions. It retains
the separate historical `--before` failure contract. Native collectors use the
existing full-schema path and authenticate endpoint ownership while the writer
is alive; source and artifact identities are held and checked again before
completion. The original preload is retained as provenance, while the native
daemon uses the receive wrapper rather than executing Python or loading that
preload.

The reviewed gate passed seven interrupted-controller tests, eight predecessor
statistics-controller tests, 57 shared CI-policy tests, and scoped strict
Clippy. Permanent regressions cover the original argparse help/error and
`--before` positions, plus leader SIGINT at an acknowledged final stdout pipe
write after all five worker results. Final stdout is fallible and precedes root
receipt publication; cancellation cannot leave that controlled boundary marked
successful. Existing foreign receipts are never overwritten or removed.

The same eight frozen artifacts passed all four native checker CLIs before and
after removing exactly `check_stats_interrupted.py` and `stats_source.py`:
five interrupted cases, one ordinary daemon case, eight startup-failure cases,
and one log-fault case (15 per phase). Each phase ran with an empty PATH and
recorded 50 execve attempts, all to the sealed native artifact paths, with no
Python attempts. Four normalized reports were byte-identical. Eleven receipt
source-hash maps changed only by omission of the two retired originals; every
retained source and artifact hash stayed identical. Original source bytes were
verified against their Git blobs and independently captured pins, then archived
read-only before deletion. They were not restored or executed afterward.

Private evidence is indexed by `FINAL-HANDOFF.json` in the scratch directory
above, with the before/after audits in `frozen-EwY6f6FE`. The fresh post-deletion
gate passed 72 tests (7 interrupted,8 predecessor,44 CI policy,13 disk) and strict
Clippy. Four checker ELFs, the producer and preload match the frozen artifacts.
Both rebuilt daemon variants differ only in the embedded logging source commit
and GNU build-id; all other bytes match. See `postdelete-proof.json`. These are host
QA results, not device validation or a claim about all statistics consumers.
